what_its_for: Rozanolixizumab-noli is used to treat generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adults who have a positive anti-AChR or anti-MuSK antibody test. Myasthenia gravis is a condition where your immune system attacks the connections between your nerves and muscles, causing muscle weakness. This medicine works by blocking a protein called FcRn, which helps reduce the harmful antibodies that are causing your muscle weakness.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a slow injection under your skin (subcutaneous infusion) using an infusion pump. It is typically given by a healthcare provider or trained caregiver. The infusion is usually given once a week. Each infusion takes about 30 to 90 minutes to complete. It is injected into the stomach area (abdomen), thigh, or upper arm. Never inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or hard. Rotate your injection sites each week.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your body weight. The usual dose is either 600 mg or 840 mg given once a week by subcutaneous infusion. Do not change your dose or stop using this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, contact your healthcare provider as soon as possible to reschedule. Try to give the missed dose within 3 days of the scheduled day. If more than 3 days have passed, skip the missed dose and resume your regular weekly schedule. Do not give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store Rystiggo in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not shake the vials. If needed, you may store it at room temperature up to 77°F (25°C) for no more than 6 weeks. Once removed from the refrigerator, use it within 6 weeks or by the expiration date, whichever comes first. Keep it out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines while taking this medicine, as it may affect how well your immune system responds and could increase your risk of infection. Talk to your doctor about any vaccines you may need before starting treatment. Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections, as this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, as this can be a side effect.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, cough, or painful urination; signs of meningitis such as severe headache, stiff neck, sensitivity to light, nausea, vomiting, or confusion; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, trouble breathing, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; unusual dizziness or extreme fatigue; or any worsening of your myasthenia gravis symptoms. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before starting this medicine.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice improvement in your muscle strength and myasthenia gravis symptoms within a few weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take several weeks of regular weekly doses before you feel the full benefit. Everyone responds differently, so talk with your doctor about what to expect for your specific situation.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine is safe to use during pregnancy. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, tell your doctor before using this medicine. It is not known if rozanolixizumab-noli passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits of breastfeeding while on this medicine. Elderly Patients: No dose adjustment is required for older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age. Kidney or Liver Problems: No dose adjustments are currently recommended, but tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions you have.
